titles.title: Duke of the Polans / ruler of Poland
titles.titleCn: 波兰公爵／波兰早期统治者

events.label: Emerged as ruler of the Polan polity
events.labelCn: 成为波兰人政权的统治者
events.note: The start of his rule is conventionally placed around 960.

events.label: Married Dobrawa of Bohemia
events.labelCn: 与波希米亚的杜布拉娃结婚
events.note: The marriage allied the Piasts with the Přemyslids.

events.label: Accepted Christianity in the Baptism of Poland
events.labelCn: 接受基督教，传统上视为“波兰受洗”

events.label: Defeated Wichmann and expanded toward Pomerania
events.labelCn: 击败维希曼并向波美拉尼亚扩张

events.label: A missionary bishopric was established at Poznań
events.labelCn: 在波兹南建立传教主教区

events.label: Defeated Margrave Odo at Cedynia
events.labelCn: 在采迪尼亚战役中击败边区伯爵奥多

events.label: Fought Bohemia and extended Piast control into Silesia
events.labelCn: 与波希米亚交战并将控制扩展至西里西亚

events.label: The Dagome iudex placed his realm under papal protection
events.labelCn: 《Dagome iudex》将其领地置于教廷保护之下

events.label: Died after consolidating the early Piast state
events.labelCn: 在巩固早期皮雅斯特国家后去世

sourceNote: Polish Ministry of Education ZPE materials on Mieszko I; Widukind of Corvey and Thietmar of Merseburg used critically; modern Piast scholarship; Wikipedia as supplementary person index.
notes:
The first well-attested Piast ruler and the political founder of the Christian Polish state. His son Bolesław I later obtained the royal crown.

Confidence / caveats: Birth and accession dates are approximate. Earlier Piast ancestry comes mainly from later chronicles. The exact extent of control over Kraków/Lesser Poland by 992 and the purpose of Dagome iudex remain debated.

Unlinked family: Siemomysł (traditional attribution) (not uniquely matched in the roster); Dobrawa of Bohemia (not uniquely matched in the roster); Oda of Haldensleben (not uniquely matched in the roster); Mieszko (not uniquely matched in the roster); Lambert (not uniquely matched in the roster); Świętopełk (not uniquely matched in the roster).

events.labelCn: 签订梅泽堡和约

events.label: Won the Peace of Bautzen
events.labelCn: 签订包岑和约并保住西部成果

events.label: Captured Kyiv during an expedition into Rus'
events.labelCn: 远征罗斯并攻占基辅

events.label: Was crowned the first King of Poland
events.labelCn: 加冕为首位波兰国王

events.label: Died shortly after his coronation
events.labelCn: 加冕后不久去世

sourceNote: Polish ZPE materials on Bolesław Chrobry; Thietmar of Merseburg and Gallus Anonymus used critically; modern Polish medieval scholarship; Wikipedia as supplementary chronology index.
notes:
Bolesław I transformed Mieszko's principality into a major Central European monarchy and became the first crowned king of Poland.

Confidence / caveats: Birth is generally 966/967. The exact boundaries of his Moravian and Slovak holdings are debated. The coronation of 1025 is secure, but its exact day is not.

notes:
Mieszko II inherited the crown but lost Bolesław I's gains under foreign and dynastic pressure. His son Casimir I later restored the state without restoring the crown.

Confidence / caveats: The 1031–1033 sequence is source-poor and complex. Mieszko's mutilation is reported by Cosmas of Prague. Exact death cause is unknown.

A short-lived Piast usurper whose seizure of power interrupted Mieszko II's kingship.

Confidence / caveats: Birth and maternal identification are uncertain. Connections between his rule and the wider 'pagan reaction' are debated.

Casimir rebuilt the Piast state after the 1030s collapse but did not revive the royal crown.

events.labelCn: 与克拉科夫主教斯坦尼斯瓦夫发生致命冲突

events.labelCn: 被废黜并遭流放

events.label: Died in exile
events.labelCn: 在流亡中去世

sourceNote: Gallus Anonymus; later traditions on Bishop Stanislaus used critically; Polish ZPE materials; modern Piast scholarship; Wikipedia as supplementary index.
notes:
Bolesław II restored the Polish royal title in 1076 but lost his throne after the crisis surrounding Bishop Stanislaus. His younger brother Władysław Herman then ruled as duke.

Confidence / caveats: The circumstances of Bishop Stanislaus's death are among the most contested episodes in early Polish history. Bolesław's exact death place and even death year have competing traditions.

notes:

Confidence / caveats: His reign was heavily influenced by the palatine Sieciech. The exact constitutional status of the territorial assignments to his sons should not be read as a modern partition treaty.

notes:
Bolesław III was the last ruler before the formal Piast fragmentation. His 1138 testament created hereditary districts plus a seniorate centered on Kraków.

Confidence / caveats: The testament's exact legal text does not survive and its reconstruction depends on later evidence. Casimir II may have been born after or shortly before his father's death, explaining his omission from the original allocation.

notes:
Przemysł II restored the Polish royal title in 1295 without controlling all former Polish lands. His kingdom centered on Greater Poland and Pomerelia, providing an ideological precedent for later reunification under Władysław I the Elbow-high.

Confidence / caveats: His 1295 coronation did not end political fragmentation. The exact organizers of his 1296 murder remain debated; Brandenburg involvement is strongly represented in near-contemporary traditions, while accusations against Greater Polish noble families are less certain. Allegations that he ordered Ludgarda's death are unproven.
